stem.text: The graph of f', the derivative of a function f, is shown for \( 0 \le x \le 6 \) and consists of six line segments. Find all values of x in the open interval \( 0 < x < 6 \) at which the graph of f has a point of inflection. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The graph of f has points of inflection exactly at \( x = 1 \) and \( x = 4 \), because f' changes between increasing and decreasing at each of these values.

worked_solution.text: The graph of f changes concavity exactly where f' changes between increasing and decreasing, which on this graph happens at a corner where a rising segment meets a falling one.
worked_solution.rule_named: inflection where the derivative changes monotonicity

worked_solution.text: Those corners are at \( x = 1 \) and \( x = 4 \), so the graph of f has a point of inflection there and nowhere else in \( 0 < x < 6 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: read the corners from the graph

options.label: The graph of f has points of inflection exactly at \( x = \frac{3}{5} \), \( x = \frac{5}{2} \) and \( x = 5 \), because f' is equal to 0 at each of these values.
options.derivation: every zero of the plotted curve f' listed as a point of inflection, with no change in concavity checked

options.label: The graph of f has points of inflection exactly at \( x = 1 \) and \( x = 4 \), because f' changes between increasing and decreasing at each of these values.
The graph of f has points of inflection exactly at \( x = 1 \), \( x = 2 \), \( x = 4 \) and \( x = 5 \), because the slope of the graph of f' changes at each of these values.
options.derivation: every corner of the graph of f' listed, including one where f' keeps rising or keeps falling and only its steepness changes

options.label: The graph of f has exactly one point of inflection, at \( x = 1 \), because f' changes between increasing and decreasing there.
options.derivation: the corner at x = 4, where f' changes between increasing and decreasing, omitted from the list

figure.alt: The graph of f' is made of line segments joining (0, 3), (1, -2), (2, -1), (3, 1), (4, 3), (5, 0), (6, -1).
